_comment: Partner referral node registry. Ratified by Jason, 2026-09-14 (registry v3.63).
SIGNED PARTNERS ONLY. A slug is a branded link the partner puts their name next to,
so issuing one to a node still in negotiation tells them they are a partner before
they have agreed to be one. Jason's rule: signed first, slug after. Nodes in
negotiation get a slug the day they sign -- one line here plus p/index.html.
NOTE ON CANON: the marketics-canon skill labels some nodes '(partner)' that are NOT
signed -- STR Cribs among them. In that row 'partner' denotes a relationship, not an
agreement. Do not derive this file from that row; it was tried on 2026-09-14 and
produced referral links for four nodes still in negotiation.
ORGANISATION LABELS ONLY -- NO PERSON NAMES, DELIBERATELY. Two reasons, both load-
bearing: (1) scripts/ is not blocked from the web, so this file is fetchable, and the
person-to-node mapping is relationship structure canon keeps private for some nodes;
(2) that mapping already lives in canon's stakeholder rows, and a second copy of a
canon row is a defect rather than a convenience (registry v3.62). Look the contact up
in canon; do not restate one here.
Slug rules: lowercase, [a-z0-9-], STABLE FOREVER once issued. A slug appears in
reporting and in the link the partner themselves holds, so renaming one silently
splits that node's history in two.

slug_issued is the date THIS FILE issued the slug. It is NOT the signing date --
     that is not recorded here because it was not supplied, and a plausible wrong date
     is worse than an absent one (registry v3.52).
RETIRED 2026-09-16: 'pricelabs'. It fails the bundled-tool test -- an owner would never buy
PriceLabs separately from Marketics, because the listing sits inside the service and runs on
Marketics' own account. No outbound referral direction exists, so no ladder rung can ever be
owed on it; the relationship runs the other way, with Marketics in THEIR partner program.
/p/pricelabs still FORWARDS: an unknown slug reaches /get-started unstamped rather than
404ing, so anyone already holding the link still lands. They are simply uncounted. That is
the correct failure direction -- never lose the visitor for the sake of the record -- and it
is deliberate, not a leftover.
